sections.summary: Paul declares the Corinthians themselves are his letter of recommendation, a letter of Christ written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on hearts of flesh, echoing the new covenant promises of Jeremiah 31:33 and Ezekiel 36:26.

sections.section_title: Sufficiency from God and the Ministry of the New Covenant
sections.summary: Paul answers the sufficiency question from 2:16 by denying self-sufficiency and identifying God as the one who qualified him to be a minister of a new covenant characterized not by the written code (gramma) that kills but by the Spirit (pneuma) who gives life.

sections.section_title: The Greater Glory -- Two Ministries Compared
sections.summary: Through three lesser-to-greater (qal wahomer) arguments, Paul demonstrates that the new covenant ministry surpasses the Sinai covenant ministry in glory, contrasting the ministry of death with the ministry of the Spirit, the ministry of condemnation with the ministry of righteousness, and the transient with the permanent.

sections.section_title: Boldness, the Veil, and Hardened Minds
sections.summary: Paul claims boldness (parresia) for his ministry in contrast to Moses who veiled his face to conceal the fading of the old covenant's glory, then describes a veil persisting over the hearts of those who hear Moses read without turning to the Lord, a veil removed only in Christ.

sections.section_title: The Lord, the Spirit, Freedom, and Transformation
sections.summary: Paul identifies the Lord encountered in the new covenant as the Spirit who brings freedom from the veiled condition, and declares that the entire community with unveiled face, beholding the Lord's glory, is being progressively transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another by the Lord who is the Spirit.
